bull_bear.body:
- integration: Backward-integrated operations spanning intermediates, technicals and formulations, giving control over cost, quality and supply reliability — evidence: Unit-IV manufactures Liquid Bromine, Phenol, Ammonium Chloride Powder, Poly Ammonium Chloride, Copper Hydroxide, Bromobenzene and Pure Benzene, enabling the Company to become self-dependent mainly for Bromine recovery.

bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Cyclical, weather-dependent demand — Demand for agrochemicals is closely linked to the agricultural sector and sensitive to weather variables (droughts, floods, uneven rainfall); prolonged adverse conditions in key markets can defer or reduce consumption.
- Global supply / Chinese pricing dynamics — Industry pricing is exposed to global supply dynamics, particularly Chinese production and inventory cycles, which can compress realisations even in periods of healthy volume growth.
- Input / raw-material dependence — A meaningful share of raw materials is imported, and geopolitical disruptions can affect availability and cost; mitigated through supplier diversification, inventory planning and backward integration.
- Export / currency and regulatory-timeline exposure — Export orientation brings exposure to currency movements and to country-specific regulatory and registration timelines.
- Contamination, adulteration and tampering risk — Given the nature of its products, the Company faces risks relating to contamination, adulteration and tampering during manufacturing, transportation and storage, which could result in product liability claims, recalls or reputational damage.
- Regulatory risk across product registrations — Spans product registrations, environmental norms and evolving pesticide legislation in India and export markets, managed through a dedicated regulatory affairs and registration function.
- Liquidity / cash-flow risk — Cash flow limitations, financial constraints and solvency pressures are flagged as a risk type in the Company's risk-management framework.
- Logistics / third-party transport reliance — Reliance on third-party transport and logistics solutions across road, rail, sea and air exposes the Company to logistics disruption.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

outlook.body:
- Strategic entry into the crop nutrition segment as a natural extension of the agri-input business, pursued through product innovation, market expansion and farmer-centric solutions.
- Strengthening global presence across key international markets, including evaluating a foreign subsidiary for regional expansion.
- Driving manufacturing excellence by leveraging existing production facilities and expanding Contract Manufacturing Organization (CMO) capabilities.
- Investing in talent acquisition and capability building, sales and marketing infrastructure, last-mile farmer engagement and channel-partner engagement to support expansion.
- Continued focus on improving operational efficiency, optimising cost structures and enhancing productivity to drive sustainable growth and margin expansion.
- Group-level focus on improving capacity utilisation and operational efficiencies across subsidiaries following recently commissioned expansion projects.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The major CAPEX programmes at Sarigam and Saykha stand concluded, with the enlarged capacities they created now in operation and fully operational as of FY26. During the year, Heranba commissioned a new pilot plant facility at Sarigam adding the capability to test formulations at bench scale, strengthening quality assurance and the Company's first-time-right approach to product development. The Sarigam technical plant (HOPL) houses 9,600 MTPA of intermediates and technical products capacity under Phase 1, with Phase 2 adding a further 9,000 MTPA of advanced agrochemical technicals, taking the total to 18,600 TPA — this Phase 2 addition is now complete and operational. The Saykha unit (HOPL) manufactures specific and non-specific herbicides and other key intermediates with an installed capacity of 6,000 MTPA, featuring hydrogenation and nitration facilities for value-added products. The Company also has 71,958 sq mt of additional area available for future expansion beyond the 1,24,970 sq mt currently in use across its 7 facilities.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Revenue growth in FY26 was driven by strong volume expansion in the domestic market, particularly the technical segment, supported by newly commissioned capacities, with export formulations lending further support.
- Industry-wide pricing pressure limited translation of volume growth into revenue growth and compressed EBITDA margin.
- Near-term domestic demand remains challenging: crop prices have stayed range-bound, and higher fertiliser costs (driven by the Middle East conflict) have raised working-capital requirements and constrained farmer liquidity, likely keeping farmers value-conscious on crop-protection purchases.
- Company expects a gradual normalisation in industry pricing, supported by China's removal of VAT export rebates on several pesticide-related products from April 2026, narrowing the pricing differential with Indian producers and improving pricing discipline globally.
- With capacities now fully operational, management expects utilisation to improve, supported by a wider product portfolio and a growing registration base across domestic and developed markets, making operating leverage increasingly visible as pricing and demand normalise.
- Company's backward-integrated manufacturing model, where cost competitiveness is critical, is expected to benefit from the improving competitive environment versus Chinese exporters.
- Consolidated profitability was impacted by losses in subsidiary operations (particularly Heranba Organics Private Limited), reflecting higher depreciation and finance costs from recently commissioned expansion projects and sub-optimal utilisation of installed capacity.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

capex_expansion.body: The major CAPEX programmes at Sarigam and Saykha stand concluded, with the enlarged capacities they created now in operation and fully operational as of FY26. During the year, Heranba commissioned a new pilot plant facility at Sarigam adding the capability to test formulations at bench scale, strengthening quality assurance and the Company's first-time-right approach to product development. The Sarigam technical plant (HOPL) houses 9,600 MTPA of intermediates and technical products capacity under Phase 1, with Phase 2 adding a further 9,000 MTPA of advanced agrochemical technicals, taking the total to 18,600 TPA — this Phase 2 addition is now complete and operational. The Saykha unit (HOPL) manufactures specific and non-specific herbicides and other key intermediates with an installed capacity of 6,000 MTPA, featuring hydrogenation and nitration facilities for value-added products. The Company also has 71,958 sq mt of additional area available for future expansion beyond the 1,24,970 sq mt currently in use across its 7 facilities.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Cautiously optimistic; acknowledges near-term headwinds but confident in pricing bottoming and FY26 recovery; emphasizes registration pipeline and capacity utilization as key drivers

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- integration: Backward-integrated operations spanning intermediates, technicals and formulations, giving control over cost, quality and supply reliability — evidence: Unit-IV manufactures Liquid Bromine, Phenol, Ammonium Chloride Powder, Poly Ammonium Chloride, Copper Hydroxide, Bromobenzene and Pure Benzene, enabling the Company to become self-dependent mainly for Bromine recovery.
- scale: One of the largest domestic producers of synthetic pyrethroids — evidence: recognised as such in the Company Overview, in a market where insecticides dominate Indian consumption.
- distribution: Wide international presence — evidence: exports to markets across the Middle East, the CIS, Asia, Southeast Asia and Africa, and 28.47% of turnover from exports across 85 countries, per BRSR.

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Pricing volatility in export markets; Delay in product registrations; Overcapacity in Indian agrochemical sector; Inventory gluts in global distribution channels; Execution risk at new greenfield facility (Saykha)

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Daikaffil's R&D setup could become a future revenue stream via third-party contract manufacturing; US registrations secured in Q3 are a hidden catalyst for FY26 export growth

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Strategic entry into the crop nutrition segment as a natural extension of the agri-input business, pursued through product innovation, market expansion and farmer-centric solutions.
- Strengthening global presence across key international markets, including evaluating a foreign subsidiary for regional expansion.

one-line thesis: Heranba's FY25 is a transition year with suppressed margins due to new plant under-absorption and export pricing pressure, but FY26 growth is expected to be driven by commissioning of Sarigam (Phase II) and Saykha facilities, improved pricing, and registration-led volume expansion.
financial scorecard: Revenue: Rs. 1,075cr (9M FY25) +7.5% YoY; EBITDA: Rs. 117cr (9M FY25) / 11% margin (down from 13-14% in H1); PAT: Rs. 44cr (9M FY25) +25.7% YoY (normalized: ~Rs. 50cr excluding Rs. 15-20cr fixed cost absorption); Order book: Not disclosed; Net debt: Rs. 300cr
guidance: Revenue growth: 35-40% YoY in FY26 (targeting Rs. 1,850-1,950cr); EBITDA margin: 12-14% in FY26; Order inflow: Expected to improve with new registrations; Capex/commissioning: Sarigam Phase II and Saykha to be fully operational by March 2025
segment / subsidiary detail: Technical segment impacted by export pricing (down 2-3% gross margin); Formulations growing due to value-addition; Daikaffil contributed Rs. 3.5cr in Q3 with ramp-up planned; Export revenue ~50% of total; Domestic demand improving in Q4

capex / expansion: Rs. 425cr deployed over last 2 years; Additional Rs. 50-100cr expected for final phase of Sarigam and Saykha; Total capex cycle nearing completion by March 2025
capital allocation: Debt repayment prioritized (net debt Rs. 300cr); No dividend policy disclosed; Future capex minimal; Focus on operational efficiency and registration-driven revenue growth

themes.title: Agrochemicals & crop-input cycle recovery
themes.need: Crop-protection is recovering off a brutal trough, and Q1FY27 shows domestic branded volume decoupling from generic exports. RALLIS grew revenue only 7% yet lifted EBITDA 23% to a ~18.0% margin (+230bps) as domestic B2C rose 19% on +15% volume while exports COLLAPSED 28% (volume -35%) on Chinese pricing, and its seeds EBITDA margin went 26% to 30% on a rice/maize/millet mix versus price-controlled cotton - though PAT +31% is flattered by an INR 35cr employee-provision reversal of which INR 24cr is genuinely one-time, so normalise before extrapolating. The monsoon is the live variable: as of 8-Jul seasonal rainfall was ~15% below normal with kharif acreage ~21% below last year. SUMICHEM delivered record FY26 profitability; INSECTICID/DHANUKA/SHARDACROP ride premiumization + technicals; COROMANDEL/GNFC/CHAMBLFERT/GODREJAGRO add fertilizers + integrated agri.
themes.driver: Monsoon catch-up and kharif acreage recovery from ~21% below last year; domestic B2C volume against continued Chinese export price pressure; new molecule launches and biologicals scale-up.

hero.oneLiner: Heranba Industries is among India's leading agrochemical companies, manufacturing across the full value chain from intermediates and technical-grade products to finished formulations, and is recognised as one of the largest domestic producers of synthetic pyrethroids.
